title: Token Ark — Pricing Palette and Export Flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, role-aware pricing palette and CSV/NDJSON export flow for token-level cost analytics in the Redwood Console. The scope covers: (1) an in-dashboard pricing palette that surfaces per-route and per-model unit costs, quantization/variant deltas, and amortized cache/batching adjustments; (2) a lightweight attribution panel to map token spend to customer metadata (route, user_role, session_id); (3) a flexible export builder (CSV + NDJSON) with schema presets and a masking option for PII-sensitive fields. Deliverables: Figma prototypes (desktop + narrow desktop), a developer-facing export spec, acceptance criteria and accessibility checklist, and one usability test report with customers from two pilot accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing palette displays per-token cost, effective per-message cost, and percent delta against baseline for selected model variants
Attribution panel can group by route, model, user_role, and session and export aggregated or raw token rows
Export builder supports CSV with column order presets and NDJSON with nested attribution arrays (flattening optional)
Design implemented with color/contrast meeting WCAG AA for new visual elements
Prototype validated in 5 moderated sessions and at least one engineering feasibility review completed
dev_notes: Engineers: export should support streaming NDJSON with backpressure support; CSV must include explicit header mapping and a stable row id. Export should accept a date-range and optional filter expressions (route="/api/chat" AND user_role!="system") and return a signed URL for download. Keep payloads under 500MB by default; for larger exports return a job id and storage location. Include tokenization details: unit_token_count, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, kv_cache_saved_tokens. See GH issue ENG-4621 for batching constraints.
review_feedback: PM (Linh Tran): prioritize aggregated presets for enterprise users; single-click export of monthly invoice bundle
Eng (Sana Iqbal): keep client-visible schema flat for CSV; NDJSON for internal analysis only
Security (Roberto Moreno): add masking option for fields user_email and user_ip; require opt-in for raw exports
Design (Clara Wong): palette colors should map to existing cost semantic tokens (increase/decrease/neutral) and avoid new hues
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff complete; explored 3 layout directions (compact matrix, timeline stripe, stacked ledger)
2026-02-28: Selected compact matrix + drawer attribution as primary pattern after PM/Eng sync
2026-03-03: First prototype shared with pilot customers (Acme AI, FinLy); received request for role-based presets
2026-03-09: Engineering feasibility review — agreed on export job service and signed URL approach; noted quota implications for large historical exports
2026-03-12: Usability test (5 participants) — users appreciated per-variant delta but asked for clearer definition of "amortized cache" metric
2026-03-14: Updated prototype to include context tooltip and new header row with stable IDs for CSV
decisions: Use compact matrix layout as default with a collapsible right-hand attribution drawer
CSV schema will be flat; NDJSON will be available as an opt-in advanced export
Masking for PII fields is opt-out for enterprise admins; raw exports require documented justification
Show percent delta against a configured baseline model (default: gf-1.0) with a control to change baseline at the top of the palette
next_steps: Finalize export schema and publish dev-facing spec (target 2026-03-18)
Implement small pilot A/B: compact matrix vs stacked ledger for power users (ENG-4789)
Add glossary tooltip for amortized cache and batching savings (Design + Docs)
Coordinate with Billing to include monthly preset for invoice-ready exports
usability_findings: Participants confused by 'amortized cache' label — preferred 'cache savings (tokens)'
Need explicit sample rows when users choose 'raw tokens' export to understand column meaning
Power users asked for field-level toggles and an easy way to save export presets
export_spec: CSV columns (stable order): export_id, export_date, route, model, model_variant, baseline_model, user_role, session_id, message_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, kv_cache_saved_tokens, unit_token_cost_cents, total_message_cost_cents, batch_id (if applicable). NDJSON option: one object per message with attribution array for per-token provenance. Include metadata header with schema version and baseline hash.
accessibility_notes: Color semantics must meet 4.5:1 contrast for delta badges. Keyboard focus should expose drawer controls and export presets. Screenreader: announce export job creation and provide link to job status. Add aria-labels for all toggle buttons and ensure CSV download link has descriptive text.
